New York Senator Chuck Schumer’s post is misleading and politically opportunistic. The House Republican budget proposal does not “eliminate the CDC’s HIV prevention budget.” It consolidates several overlapping CDC programs (including HIV, viral hepatitis, TB, and STD prevention) into a single block grant to give states more flexibility, while actually increasing overall funding** for these infectious-disease efforts compared to the Senate Democrat level. Specifically, the House bill provides $1.22 billion for the new consolidated block grant, an increase of roughly $47 million over current HIV-specific funding alone.
States would still be required to maintain robust HIV prevention, testing, and surveillance, and partner-services programs to receive the funds.
PEPFAR (the hugely successful global AIDS program Schumer often praises) is fully funded and untouched. Claiming Republicans want to “eliminate” lifesaving HIV programs on #WorldAIDSDay is the same tired scare tactic Democrats use every budget cycle. People living with HIV deserve honest policy debates, not inflammatory tweets that distort the facts for partisan gain. We can modernize how we deliver prevention and care without slashing funding, and that’s exactly what the House proposal does. Democrats should negotiate in good faith instead of fearmongering.
